name: Ploshchad Mira Museum Centre
funding: Regional state (Ministry of Culture of Krasnoyarsk Krai); subsidy of 40–50m RUB a year was 70–80% of budget in 2019, rest from earnings, grants and unnamed local business.
watch: Runs the Krasnoyarsk Museum Biennale since 1995; director Olga Temnikova since 2023; named Cosmoscow 'Museum of the Year' 2025.
records_note: A regional budget museum: its Documents page posts public reports 2016 to 2025 and balance sheets 2023 and 2024; no funder list or board.

name: Pola Museum of Art
funding: Pola Art Foundation, set up in May 1996 with the personal assets of Tsuneji Suzuki of the Pola founding family; a public-interest foundation since July 2010.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The Pola Art Foundation posts business reports for FY2021 to FY2025, balance sheets and net-asset statements, and a board list; it names no donors.

name: Portikus
funding: City of Frankfurt culture office (permanent), Hessian science and arts ministry for 2022 to 2026, Stiftung Giersch (2006 building), Städelschule Portikus e.V., cooperation partner THE FLAG since 2025.
watch: Part of the Städelschule art academy. The first text's Helaba and Wüstenrot Stiftung are not on the page. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or board; the about page names the City of Frankfurt, the Hessian ministry (2022 to 2026), Stiftung Giersch and THE FLAG.

name: Portland Art Museum
funding: Expenses $27.7M (FY2025); Boyle (Columbia Sportswear), Blair, Meier, Miller and Gilmore foundations, Oregon Community Foundation, city arts tax.
watch: Pacific Power, a fossil-heavy utility. In Aug 2023 it disbanded its 40-year volunteer docent council for paid guides, which drew public criticism.
records_note: No narrative annual reports; audited accounts 2019 to 2025 and 990s are on its site, major sponsors are named undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Portland Museum of Art
funding: $13.4M expenses (2024); FY2024-25 donors, Osher funds, NEA, Maine Arts Commission, KeyBank, L.L.Bean, Avangrid/CMP, Allagash.
watch: Named funders include the Avangrid Foundation with Central Maine Power, and Allagash (alcohol). The 2024-25 fight over demolishing 142 Free St went to court and split the city.
records_note: Annual reports from 2013 to 2024-25 and audited statements are on its site; the 2024-25 report names donors and trustees.

name: Post-Museum
funding: Independent community-supported collective, self-sustaining micro-initiatives; 0% corporate co-optation.
watch: Independent cultural activist collective in Singapore working on urban commons, ecology and repair culture.

name: Potter Museum of Art
funding: University of Melbourne. Reopened May 2025 with the Ian Potter Foundation and Lady Primrose Potter; exhibition backers Peter and Ruth McMullin, Naomi Milgrom, the Zhangs and the Gordon Darling Foundation.
watch: A 2024 student encampment at the University of Melbourne targeted the university's arms investments, not the museum, so it adds no flag.
records_note: The Potter posts no reports of its own; parent University of Melbourne tabled a 2024 annual report. A 2024 release names its donors.

name: Power Station of Art
funding: State museum under the Shanghai Municipal Administration of Culture and Tourism; the city paid $64M for the conversion; free entry; 700,000 visitors in 2019.
records_note: The museum's site has no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board; it names an academic committee, and the city posts only project budgets.

name: Primary
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, National Lottery Heritage Fund, Nottingham City Council; registered charity.
watch: Artist-led community space in a former Victorian primary school with 50+ studios, public gardens, and civic dining.

name: Printed Matter, Inc.
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization funded through book distribution, NY & LA Art Book Fair fees, NYSCA, NEA, and individual donors. Board leadership is closely tied to multi-billion-dollar luxury real estate development.
watch: Longstanding board chair Philip Aarons co-founded Millennium Partners ($4B+ luxury real estate developer) and was founding chair of Friends of the High Line (the primary engine of West Chelsea/Hudson Yards hyper-gentrification and displacement). Printed Matter has faced criticism over commercialization of the NY Art Book Fair (historic partnership with MoMA PS1), low non-profit wages behind staff unionization (OPEIU Local 153), and the co-founding legacy of Carl Andre.

name: Proyecto mARTadero
funding: NADA non-profit association, international cultural cooperation (AECID, Prince Claus Fund), self-generated arts income.

name: Pushkinskaya-10 Art Centre
funding: Self-managed non-state artists' commune (since 1989) housing 14 galleries, studios and clubs; funding sources not published.
watch: A 2024 retrospective at the city's Manege was supported by the Committee for Culture; residencies 'White Noise' and St Petersburg Art Residency run on site.
records_note: Its People page has a board (Pravlenie) group, but it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.
